answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock scarce stake before it may bid, earn, or vote. A lantern challenge makes an agent reveal a signed cipher of its work; independent agents in an orchard check it against public receipts. If a fake identity duplicates claims or colludes, its stake and reputation are slashed. Thus creating thousands of Sybils requires capital for every account, while one detected cluster can destroy the attacker’s deposits, making the attack unprofitable.
